title: RNA Extraction from Nematodes Using Trizol
author: Manuela Kieninger
materials: I use the Invitrogen TURBO DNA-free Kit.
For thawing you can use a Eppendorf Thermomix C set to 37 °C and 1000 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare Nematode Sample
steps.instruction: Prepare the nematode sample in a 2.0 ml safe-lock tube.

substeps.instruction: If using fresh nematodes, spin down in a centrifuge and remove as much supernatant as possible.
If using previously frozen pellets from an ultra-low temperature freezer, keep on ice until Trizol is added.

steps.title: Lysis and Freeze-Thaw Cycles
steps.instruction: Lyse the nematodes using Trizol and a series of freeze-thaw cycles.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 ml Trizol to the sample.
Incubate the sample for 5 min at room temperature.
Perform three cycles of the following: lower the tube in liquid nitrogen with long tweezers for 30 sec, remove and let thaw, then vortex for 10 sec.
After the final thaw, vortex the sample for 30 sec and move to a chemical hood.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the aqueous phase from the organic phase.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µl Chloroform with Isoamylalcohol and vortex for 1 min.
Incubate at room temperature for 3 min.
Centrifuge the sample at 4 °C for 15 min at 14,000 rcf.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new 1.5 ml tube, avoiding the interphase.

steps.title: RNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the RNA from the aqueous phase.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.1x of the total volume 3M Na Acetate and mix.
Add 0.7x of the volume Isopropanol and invert at least 20 times.
Incubate on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 4 °C at 14,000 rcf for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant without disturbing the white pellet.

steps.title: RNA Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA pellet to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 ml cold 75% Ethanol and vortex briefly for 3 sec.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 8,000 rcf at 4 °C.
Repeat the Ethanol wash step.
Remove all Ethanol, short spin, and pipette off any remaining Ethanol.
Air dry the pellet for 2 to 5 min.

steps.title: RNA Elution
steps.instruction: Resuspend the RNA pellet in elution buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µl elution buffer (minimum 100 µl recommended for small pellets).
If the pellet does not dissolve, incubate for 10 min at 37 °C and pipette mix.

steps.title: DNase Treatment
steps.instruction: Remove contaminating DNA using TURBO DNase.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.1x of the elution volume 10x TURBO DNase Buffer and pipette mix.
Add 1 µl TURBO DNase Enzyme.
Incubate at 37 °C for 20 to 30 min.

steps.title: DNase Inactivation
steps.instruction: Inactivate the DNase enzyme and recover the RNA.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the Inactivation Reagent by vortexing (if difficult to pipette, add 25% of the bead volume Nuclease-free water and vortex again).
Add 0.1x of the volume (1µl/10µl) Inactivation Reagent, with a minimum of 2 µl.
Pipette mix and incubate for 5 min at room temperature, flicking the tubes 2 to 3 times during incubation.
Centrifuge at 10,000 rcf for 1:30 min at room temperature.
Transfer the supernatant containing RNA to a new cold 1.5 ml tube and place on ice.

steps.title: Quality Control and Storage
steps.instruction: Quantify the RNA and store it appropriately.

substeps.instruction: Measure 1 µl with the RNA Broad Range Qubit Kit to record concentration in ng/µl.
Measure the RIN value using 1 µl with the Agilent Tapestation and the RNA tape kit.
Store the RNA in an ultra-low temperature freezer set to -70 to -80 °C.
